transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-17 14:00 PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen, Marcus Hale, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Priya Raman, Evan Liu, Sarah Gomez, Tom Becker (Aegis)

Summary: quick run-through of network topology, then live Q&A and lab-style troubleshooting. Marcus to demo a PrivateLink attach and show KV cache latency numbers under simulated egress constraints.

---
00:00:03 Laura (Redwood AE): ok folks, thanks for joining everyone, um, we wanted to keep this pretty hands on — we're going to start with the target topology you sent over, and then walk through where latency tends to show up with inference workloads
00:00:18 Priya (Aegis CTO): sounds good, we have about 30 minutes of context and then we wanted to dive into the lab, we sent the diagram in the invite, hope that helps
00:00:27 Marcus (Redwood SE): yep we have it, thanks. quick call out, i'll focus on PrivateLink attachment patterns and the egress hairpin/NAT behavior — diego will cover runtime tuning and KV cache impacts later
00:00:40 Evan (Aegis Infra): quick note: our prod VPC is NAT gw behind TGW, MTU is currently 1500, and we do have strict egress inspection via a proxy appliance in a different AZ
00:00:52 Sarah (Aegis Security): and we need to confirm encryption at rest + KMS integration for dedicated instances, also audit logs forwarded to our ELK
00:01:05 Laura: great. quick agenda — 1) PrivateLink and route table patterns, 2) DNS and Route53 resolver behavior, 3) NAT/hairpin issues and how they affect KV cache/batching, 4) runtime/quantization tradeoffs, 5) next steps and pilot plan

00:04:12 Marcus: ok, so on PrivateLink there are two common patterns we recommend for Private deployment — one is endpoint-per-subnet where each customer subnet has a VPC Endpoint that terminates to our PrivateLink service; the other is centralised endpoint + TGW route propagation. each has tradeoffs.
00:04:37 Tom (Aegis ML Eng): for us, least blast radius is endpoint-per-subnet, because we segment models by subnet, but that increases number of endpoints and, you know, route table management complexity
00:04:51 Marcus: exactly. also if you're using our Dedicated pool per-model segmentation, the per-subnet endpoint gives cleaner isolation. centralised is easier for egress control and observability though.
00:05:15 Evan: when you say endpoint, do we need to open specific SG ports? we have strict SG rules
00:05:22 Marcus: yes — we recommend allowing HTTPS/443 from your app subnets to the endpoint's SG; the endpoint's SG then allows to our service side. we can provide IaC snippets for the SGs. note: if you have a proxy appliance in path, the TLS terminates there which can break mTLS unless you do tcp passthrough. we've seen cases where proxy does SNI stripping.

00:08:50 Diego (Redwood SRE): jumping into KV cache — the biggest gotcha is that KV cache hits only help if requests are routed to the same model host/backplane. if PrivateLink + TGW or NAT routes cause failover to a different AZ or a fallback model variant, you lose warm KV state and see a p99 spike.
00:09:10 Priya: so hairpinned egress — when our service calls out to the internet for auxiliary tooling — would that impact the model's KV cache?
00:09:20 Diego: indirectly, yes. the problem is request affinity. if your egress path causes the load balancer or router to reassign requests across different host pools, the runtime loses locality. also increased RTT from proxy/NAT adds per-token latency.
00:09:34 Marcus: we've measured scenarios where an extra 40-80ms of NAT/proxy RTT turned a p99 from 320ms to ~460ms for 256 token completions — mostly due to synchronous fetches for streaming handoff and smaller batching windows.

00:12:55 Evan: detail question — we saw packet drops and retransmits sometimes, is MTU mismatch a real issue? our appliances use 1400 path MTU in some paths
00:13:03 Diego: yes very much. fragmentation increases CPU in NIC and increases latency. for heavy batching (large prompt+response), we encourage path MTU consistency; we also support gRPC chunking but TLS+proxy can still fragment. if you have MTU < 1500, tell us and we'll test with smaller frame sizes in the runtime kernel.
00:13:40 Tom: ok, how about DNS? we use Route53 inbound endpoints to resolve private hostnames — will PrivateLink still need public DNS entries?
00:13:50 Marcus: you can keep private Route53 records and create a private hosted zone. for PrivateLink our service publishes VPC endpoint DNS names that resolve to the ENIs in our VPC. if you use Route53 Resolver endpoints, ensure conditional forwarding to our resolver IPs. otherwise you'll hit the public resolver and may get public IPs that break routing.

00:16:10 Sarah: can you explain the flow when we use a forward proxy — we see TLS inspection there, how does that play with the Redwood runtime's streaming?
00:16:22 Marcus: TLS inspection often breaks http/2 and streaming because it inserts buffering. streaming needs end-to-end TCP flow semantics; when proxy buffers and reassembles, it increases tail latency and can break chunked transfer semantics. if you must have inspection, we recommend whitelisting endpoint ARNs and bypassing payload inspection for inference traffic, or using a TLS passthrough to preserve mTLS between your app and our endpoint.

00:19:05 Priya: on the dedicated trial, we want to validate throughput and ensure no cold-start hit during burst periods — what's your recommended test harness?
00:19:15 Diego: we usually run a two-phase test: 1) steady-state load to measure throughput and token efficiency (batching windows, KV hit rates), 2) burst tests with sudden ramp to simulate scale-ups and see how batch accumulation and autoscaler behaves. we'll provide a script that simulates your token distribution and prompt lengths.
00:19:33 Marcus: and instrument p50/p95/p99 and KV hit ratio; if you see p99 spikes during ramp it's usually egress or affinity issues not the runtime itself.

00:22:40 Tom: quick quantization question — we plan to run some models at int8 or 4-bit quant, any gotchas on quality vs latency when you run in private?
00:22:51 Diego: quantization reduces memory and can speed things up especially for throughput-heavy workloads; however for some decoder-only models 4-bit can introduce subtle quality regressions. our Optimize tool provides per-prompt evals. note: quantized kernels may change compute pattern which interacts with dynamic batching; sometimes quantized faster per-token but batching needs to be tuned differently to avoid tail latency increases.
00:23:22 Marcus: small add — quantized models have different kernel selection; if you mix quantized and full-precision hosts in the same pool, affinity rules should pin similar requests to like hosts to avoid big variance.

00:26:02 Evan: about KV cache eviction — if we have many short-lived sessions, does that pollute the cache?
00:26:10 Diego: yes, LRU eviction will evict older prefixes. we have a configurable cache size per host; for private Dedicated pools you can increase the cache budget. also using request-level affinity (sticky sessions) helps keep hot prefixes together.

00:28:20 Marcus: demo time — i'm going to show a PrivateLink attach; please bear with the screen share. (several seconds of typing) ok — create VPCE endpoint in the us-west-2 subnet, attach SG allow 443 from app-subnet, add route table entry for 10.2.0.0/16 to point to the endpoint. after that we configure the endpoint service in our account and accept connection on our side.
00:29:05 Evan: i see, in our environment we have an enforced proxy so the VPCE attachment still goes via the proxy, which we've seen cause SNI strip. how would we side-step that?
00:29:12 Marcus: two options: 1) allow direct egress to the VPCE SG from your app subnets (bypass proxy for inference traffic), or 2) run the proxy in TCP passthrough mode for VPCE traffic so TLS isn't terminated at the proxy. Option 1 is simpler but requires exception gating.

00:31:40 Priya: what's best practice for NAT? single NAT in a public subnet vs per-AZ NATs?
00:31:48 Diego: per-AZ NATs reduce cross-AZ hairpinning and improve latency; single NAT causes egress hotspots and cross-AZ packets that break affinity. we strongly recommend per-AZ NATGW if you have AZ-isolated model hosts. Also consider SNAT port exhaustion — for high QPS we add Elastic IP pools and scale NAT instances accordingly.

00:34:50 Tom: i want to measure end-to-end token latency under two conditions — with KV warm and with cold. how do we capture that?
00:35:00 Marcus: we provide a harness that runs sequential warmup requests and then measures single request latency distribution. we'll also add instrumentation for kv_hit boolean in traces so you can filter traces. remember streaming adds a small constant overhead but lowers perceived latency for end-users.

00:37:20 Evan: any recommendations for aperture size for batching? our request size distribution is heavy on short prompts ~20-30 tokens
00:37:29 Diego: for short prompts you want smaller max batch size but aggressive batching window (10-30ms) to accumulate enough tokens. continuous batching helps — runtime fills a batch up to token budget, not just request count. for many small prompts the token budgeting approach is more efficient.

00:40:10 Laura: question from sales ops — what happens if a route table gets misconfigured and traffic egresses to public internet?
00:40:18 Marcus: then you'll hit our public hosted endpoints and may incur different routing, increased latency, and potential data egress footprints. we recommend strict route table testing in a staging VPC first. we can also provide a conditional alert that flags when requests are routing to public IPs.

00:43:05 Priya: can we pin model versions and have controlled rollouts, so we can validate KV and quantization changes gradually?
00:43:14 Laura: yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts and A/B with automatic fallback. for private Dedicated pools you can pin host pools to model revisions and apply traffic split rules. we'll include a rollout plan in the pilot doc.

00:45:50 Sarah: auditors will ask about logs — do you provide per-request audit log with identity and prompt hashes? how long retained?
00:46:00 Diego: we can forward audit logs to your S3 or SIEM; retention and redaction policies are configurable. for sensitive data we recommend hashing or redacting prompt content before forwarding; we also integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption.

00:48:30 Marcus: quick note — we've seen customers accidentally double-encrypt when proxy performs TLS termination; when that happens client cert validation can fail at our side for mTLS. best practice: either full end-to-end TLS with no interception or perform mutual TLS between app and endpoint and have proxy operate as pure TCP forwarder.

00:51:05 Tom: let's simulate a problematic path — do you have a quick test for detecting hairpin?
00:51:13 Diego: yes run traceroute from app-host to endpoint IP and check whether it traverses the NAT GW or jumps AZs. also we provide a small agent that emits a synthetic request with a header that our backplane logs and returns which host handled it so you can verify affinity.

00:54:00 Evan: we want to try the Dedicated trial next week, how long to set up?
00:54:08 Marcus: usually 24-48 hours to provision the Dedicated pool and another 24 to attach PrivateLink and validate. we'll prioritize if you sign the trial agreement.

00:55:40 Priya: any security checklist / items we need to complete before the trial?
00:55:48 Laura: yes, we'll share a short security checklist — SAML SSO integration, KMS key arn, CIDR ranges, SIEM log endpoint, and any compliance docs. Sarah, we'll route the SOC2/ISO docs to you via the share link.

01:00:02 Diego: final runtime note — for quantized models please include representative prompt sets in the evals. we can run A/B with full precision and quantized kernels and provide diff reports on token-level perplexity and sampling quality metrics. small prompt sets may not reveal edge cases.

01:03:15 Marcus: last thing — when we run the burst test, expect autoscaler to bring up hosts which causes cold KV cache, so we recommend a rolling buffer that pre-warms with a subset of traffic. we can script a warmup to reduce cold-start p99 spikes.
01:05:30 Priya: awesome — this was super helpful. recap — Laura will send runbook and pricing, Marcus will provision the Dedicated trial, Diego will provide the test harness and traceroute agent, Tom to send prompt corpus and traffic profile.
01:06:02 Laura: and we'll schedule the follow-up for a live trial run on 2027-11-24.
01:06:12 Evan: thanks everyone, we'll get the CIDRs and logs over by Monday.
01:06:25 Sarah: thanks — appreciate the clarity on TLS/proxy patterns.
01:06:40 Laura: thanks all, talk soon.
